title: Config Sync groups file (config-sync.json)
description: The groups file at <data folder>/config-sync.json. Config Sync no longer WRITES this file — since settings schema v2 the sync list is compiled from the plugin's own data.json (`items` + `custom`) — but this shape is more than a legacy reader: every compiled group passes through `parseGroup` on every recompile (src/main.ts's recompile -> src/core/manifest.ts), so it is the live internal contract for what a sync rule looks like, as well as the format of a hand-kept or pre-v2 file. This schema mirrors that validator; the validator is the authority. As of schema v3 the vocabulary matches data.json's own: `sharing` objects (not the old flat `scope` string) and `perElement` (not `perItem`).

$schema.description: Ignored by the plugin (manifest.ts proves an incoming one changes nothing); a hand-edited file may point it at this schema for editor validation.

version.description: The manifest FILE's own format version — unrelated to data.json's schemaVersion. This build only accepts 1.

groups.description: The sync rules, one object per rule. Order is not meaningful; identity is each group's `name`. validateSyncManifest additionally rejects what draft-07 cannot express: duplicate names, duplicate refs, duplicate store paths, and a custom rule that takes a reserved name at the wrong path.

items.description: additionalProperties is true here (unlike the strict per-rule shape validateSyncManifest enforces at parse time) because parseGroup validates the named fields and then CARRIES every other key on the object untouched (invariant II.1) — a field a newer build wrote survives an older build's read instead of being silently stripped.

name.description: Unique rule id. Letters, digits, "-" or "_", starting with a letter or digit (manifest.ts's GROUP_NAME_RE) — the same pattern enforced at the companion add/edit UI boundary.

path.description: Vault-relative path; {configDir} expands to this device's config dir. Must not start with "/" and must not contain a ".." path segment.

type.description: "file" or "folder" only. "dir" is NOT accepted here — that spelling exists only as a v2 settings-document literal, converted by src/core/v2Migration.ts before a value ever reaches this validator; a hand-written config-sync.json using "dir" is rejected.

devices.description: Which device CLASS this rule's whole group targets. Distinct from a field/file rule's own "sharing" — see the fieldRule/fileRule definitions.

description.description: Human-readable label for this group, shown in the settings panel. An empty or whitespace-only value is dropped by the parser (trim-and-drop), not rejected.

sanitize.description: REFUSED outright if present (not merely ignored): this is the pre-v2 `{"pattern", "action": "strip"|"encrypt"}` shape. Rename to "mode": "fields" with a "fields" rules array.

mode.description: Sync mode. Absent = "plain". "fields" (file groups only) applies per-key rules; "encrypted" encrypts the whole file.

fields.description: Per-key rules. Only valid with "mode": "fields" — present without it is rejected.

fileRule.description: Whole-file rule for a Plain single-file group ("type": "file" only — never a folder group). Never valid with "mode": "fields" or "encrypted".

perElement.description: Per-element sharing for string-array/boolean-map keys: key name -> { element value -> sharing }. Only valid with "mode": "fields"; a key listed here can never also have "encrypted": true in its own field rule (encryption stays key-level).

label.description: Display name recorded when the item is enabled or captured; shown even where the plugin isn't installed. An empty or whitespace-only value is dropped by the parser (trim-and-drop), not rejected.

origin.description: Set by the plugin for rules created from the Discovered-files section; name, path and type are fixed by the file (always a file, never a folder — the UI locks the type picker).

ref.description: This rule's item identity (src/core/types.ts's ItemRef) — the key of the store lock, the device-local baselines and the device-local opt-out list. A group the compiler produced always carries one; a hand-written rule that omits it is assigned the same ref a v1/v2 lock converter would give its name (manifest.ts's legacyRef), so it is never truly optional in practice, just optional to WRITE by hand.

allOf.description: "fields" needs "mode": "fields" — otherwise the per-key rules never take effect.
"mode": "fields" is only supported on file groups.
"perElement" needs "mode": "fields" — otherwise the per-element sharing never takes effect.
"fileRule" only applies to a single-file rule ("type": "file") in Plain mode — never a folder group, never combined with "mode": "fields" or "encrypted".

sharing.description: "Who shares a value" (src/core/types.ts's Sharing) — retired v1's flat scope enum ("all"|"desktop"|"mobile"|"local"), which collapsed two orthogonal questions (is this shared, and with whom?) into one list.

oneOf.description: Every device gets the same value.
Each device class keeps its own value in a __scopes__ sidecar.
Never leaves this device and never enters the store — v1's "local".

fieldRule.description: Sharing and encryption are independent axes, not one action enum. (Before schema v2 this was {"pattern", "action": "strip"|"encrypt"}; that shape is rejected — see the top-level "sanitize" property. Before schema v3 this was {"pattern", "scope", "encrypted"}; "scope" strings are no longer accepted, only "sharing" objects.)

encrypted.description: Whole-value encryption for the keys this pattern matches. A this-device rule can never be encrypted — nothing leaves the device for encryption to protect in transit (the `not` clause below).

locked.description: Preset rule injected by the plugin; cannot be removed in the UI.

not.description: A value that never leaves this device (sharing.kind: "this-device") has nothing to encrypt for transit.

sharing.description: No "this-device": a Plain file that should not travel is expressed by the rule's own sync toggle, not by a file-level rule.

encrypted.description: Whole-file encryption: the group's entire store copy is one encrypted envelope instead of the raw file.
